edges.description: Tick-delivered spirochetes deploy complement evasion to blunt innate killing and establish spirochetemia.
Vtp-producing spirochetes from tick salivary glands establish mammalian infection by tick bite and disseminate through the bloodstream.
Complement evasion supports survival of bloodstream Borrelia.
Bloodstream expansion creates the antigenic-variation dynamics that drive recurrent bacteremic waves.
Each bacteremic wave elicits a serotype-specific antibody response that clears the dominant serotype.
edges.target: B1b-cell IgM Clearance of Bacteremic Waves

edges.description: The spirochete burden carried in the bloodstream sets the severity of the Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction precipitated when antibiotics lyse the organisms.
Each new Vmp serotype restarts bacteremia, producing the next febrile episode.
Antibody clearance of the dominant serotype selects for spirochetes that have switched to a new Vmp, driving the next wave.

edges.description: The waxing and waning bacteremic waves present clinically as recurrent fever.
High-level bacteremia and erythrocyte clearance produce anemia.
High-level bacteremia and platelet clearance produce thrombocytopenia.

nodes.description: Anemia accompanies the high-level bacteremia of relapsing fever.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic control of the innate immune response to Borrelia hermsii influences the course of relapsing fever in inbred strains of mice.
evidence.snippet: Similar to human infection, the progression of the disease in mice was associated with thrombocytopenia and anemia.

nodes.description: Relapsing fever is treated with a tetracycline (doxycycline), penicillin, or ceftriaxone; the first dose frequently triggers a Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction.

evidence.reference_title: Louse-borne relapsing fever - report of four cases in Switzerland, June-December 2015.
evidence.snippet: All patients recovered after antibiotic treatment with ceftriaxone and/or doxycycline.

nodes.description: A T-independent B1b-cell IgM response clears the dominant Vmp serotype, ending each bacteremic wave and selecting for the next antigenic variant.

evidence.reference_title: The resolution of relapsing fever borreliosis requires IgM and is concurrent with expansion of B1b lymphocytes.
evidence.snippet: Together these results support the model that B1b cells generate the T-independent IgM required for the control and resolution of relapsing fever borreliosis.

nodes.description: Selective post-exposure prophylaxis with doxycycline after a soft-tick bite prevents tick-borne relapsing fever.

evidence.reference_title: Postexposure prophylaxis of tick-borne relapsing fever: lessons learned from recent outbreaks in Israel.
evidence.snippet: its prevention is based on heightened awareness and risk stratification by active surveillance of tick bites and selective postexposure prophylaxis (PEP) with doxycycline for tick-bitten individuals.

nodes.description: FhbA-family surface proteins recruit host factor H, using the host's complement regulator to help relapsing-fever Borrelia evade alternative complement killing during early spirochetemia.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanism of Borrelia immune evasion by FhbA-related proteins.
evidence.snippet: Important mechanism for complement evasion is acquisition of the main host complement inhibitor, factor H (FH).

evidence.reference_title: Complement factor H-binding protein, a putative virulence determinant of Borrelia hermsii, is an antigenic target for protective B1b lymphocytes.
evidence.snippet: complement factor H-binding protein (FhbA), a B. hermsii outer-surface protein and putative virulence factor that does not undergo antigenic variation and is expressed by all clinical isolates.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanism of Borrelia immune evasion by FhbA-related proteins.
evidence.snippet: Conserved FH-binding mechanism within the FhbA-family was verified by analysis of a novel FH-binding protein from B. duttonii

nodes.description: Antibiotic-induced spirochete lysis triggers a Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction, a TNF-alpha / IL-6 / IL-8 cytokine surge with sudden fever, rigors and hypotension shortly after the first dose.

evidence.reference_title: Prevention of Jarisch-Herxheimer reactions by treatment with antibodies against tumor necrosis factor alpha.
evidence.snippet: antimicrobial treatment is often followed by sudden fever, rigors, and persistent hypotension (Jarisch-Herxheimer reactions) that are associated with increases in plasma concentrations of tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-alpha), interleukin-6, and interleukin-8

nodes.description: Successive Vmp-defined bacteremic waves produce the recurring high-fever episodes separated by afebrile intervals that define relapsing fever, with macrophage-mediated erythrocyte and platelet clearance driving anemia and thrombocytopenia.

evidence.reference_title: Cis-acting DNA elements flanking the variable major protein expression site of Borrelia hermsii are required for murine persistence.
evidence.snippet: The waxing and waning fever that is characteristic of relapsing fever is a direct result of spirochetal antigenic variation and sequential immune evasion.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic control of the innate immune response to Borrelia hermsii influences the course of relapsing fever in inbred strains of mice.
evidence.snippet: Relapsing fever is associated with high-level bacteremia, as well as hematologic manifestations, such as thrombocytopenia

evidence.snippet: the spirochetes repeatedly evade the host's acquired immune response by undergoing antigenic variation of the variable major proteins (Vmps) produced on their outer surface

evidence.snippet: The mutant lacking a Vmp constitutively produced Vtp, was attenuated in mice, produced lower cell densities in blood, and was unable to relapse in animals after its initial spirochetemia.
